title: Getting hired for the boat with his friend William Granger
summary: The boat needed a trumpet and clarinet; Jones refused to go without his buddy William Granger, so the leader took both trumpets.

story.theme_name: First paying gigs: getting started as a young professional
story.community_name: First paid gigs: pay, bands and young beginnings

blocks.x: About 1928, and the guy come through there and he says -- he was around the Musicians' Club there, and he was asking -- they need a trumpet player and a clarinet. They

only had one trumpet. And so they said, "Well, there's a kid around here who plays pretty good trumpet. Maybe he'll go, he'll take it." "His name is Jonah Jones. He'll be coming by here after awhile. Maybe --," so I went by, and the guy asked me about it, and I had a close friend in the band, sitting right next to me. His name was William Granger, and he played beautiful horn, beautiful trumpet, you know. I liked his playing. And we were buddies. And so the guy asked me would I go. Well, now, I didn't know how my people were going to feel about this, you know. I should be on my own, but they never felt like that, you know. So I was a little afraid to go by myself, so I told them that I'll go if you take my buddy, you know, my friend William Granger, you know. He said, "What do you play?" I said trumpet. He said, "Oh, we don't need two trumpets. All we need is one trumpet. We already have one. We're looking for a clarinet and a trumpet." I said, "Oh, no, if you can't take him I can't go." So then they went to talk to him, went to talk to Granger, and so I guess he asked the guys about Granger and they said yeah, he came out of that same band over there. He's pretty good. He can read anything you have. So they went to him. So he told them, "Well, I can't go unless you take Jonah." So finally the guy give up the idea of the clarinet, and he said, "Okay, I'll just take the two trumpets."
He already had one, and that was three, and in those days you didn't use three. Parts weren't made for three trumpets, you know.
No. And people had to do a lot of solos.
Sure, yeah. So we went on there, and it worked out all right, worked out nice, and we met some older guys, you know, that was in the band.
You felt more comfortable because you were both younger.
